title: EPA Report: Drinking Water Quality in Private Supplies | Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Ireland
description:
The EPA has just released a report that shows that private water supplies have lower water quality than public water supplies.

In 2025, 81 private water supplies were not compliant with E. coli standards.

Private water supplies include:
üö∞Small private supplies with their own well (which provide water for places like schools, nursing homes, hotels, etc.)
üö∞Private group water schemes (community run supplies)

14 (of 366) private group water schemes failed E. coli standards in 2025, down from 24 in 2024. However, 6 of these schemes had E. coli failures in both 2024 and 2025, due to ongoing issues that need to be addressed.

In 2025, almost 1 in 20 (67 of 1,623) registered small private supplies failed to meet the E. coli standard. The total number of small private supplies are unknown. Unregistered supplies are not sampled by local authorities and may unknowingly be providing unsafe drinking water to consumers.
Suppliers should register immediately to enable local authorities to monitor their supply, giving consumers confidence in the quality of their drinking water.

You can read the full report at the link in the comments.

title: Klobuchar Joins Colleagues in Introducing Legislation to Create and Expand Grant and Loan Programs to Monitor Air Pollution from Wildfires
description:
WASHINGTON - U.S. Senator Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) joined her colleagues in introducing the Wildfire Air Quality Sensor Expansion Act of 2026 to help state, local, and Tribal government agencies monitor worsening air pollution caused by wildfires and make more informed public health decisions. 

The legislation would direct the Environmental Protection Agency to create and expand new and existing grant and loan programs allowing agencies to purchase and operate portable air sensors – low-cost technology that can measure and detect harmful pollutants caused by wildfire smoke. Increasing access to air quality information will help leaders make better decisions for public health and wildfire response.

“In Minnesota, smoke from the recent wildfires in the Superior National Forest created hazy and unhealthy air quality conditions throughout the state,” said Klobuchar. “I’m supporting this legislation to help areas impacted by wildfires measure air pollutants and keep our communities healthy and safe.”

Along with Klobuchar, the legislation was introduced by Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Michael Bennet (D-CO), and Jeff Merkley (D-OR).
